members.name: Finished
members.doc: server ended the match; socket may already be gone

members.name: Lost
members.doc: transport dropped — Reconnect() resyncs

members.name: OnState
members.signature: std::function<void(const std::string& stateJson, uint64_t version)> OnState
members.doc:
Full private-view snapshot, verbatim server JSON, strictly increasing
version. Fired only for accepted (in-order) snapshots.

members.name: OnRejected
members.signature: std::function<void(uint64_t localId, const std::string& reason)> OnRejected
members.doc:
The server refused an intent: roll optimistic UI back to the last
OnState payload. localId is the value SendMove returned.

members.name: OnFinished
members.doc: Terminal result payload; the connection is done after this.

members.name: OnLost
members.doc: Transport loss (not a graceful finish) — show "reconnecting…".

members.name: Connect
members.signature: bool Connect(const std::string& gatewayUrl, const std::string& token)
members.doc:
Blocking upgrade against `<gatewayUrl>?token=<token>`. On success the
pending resync goes out immediately, which makes the gateway push full
current state — connect and reconnect are deliberately the same path.

members.name: Reconnect
members.doc:
Reconnect after Lost: same URL/token, intents queued while offline
flush after the resync in the order the user acted.

members.name: Tick
members.doc:
Pump once per frame: polls the socket, dispatches envelopes, flushes
sendable intents, keeps the heartbeat alive.

members.name: SendMove
members.doc:
Queue a move intent; `moveJson` is the envelope `data` object.
Returns the local correlation id OnRejected reports back.

members.name: SendReaction
members.doc:
Fire-and-forget reaction (emoji) — not an intent, never queued/rolled
back, silently dropped while offline.

members.name: GetSecondsSinceHeard
members.doc:
Seconds since the last pong (or connect). The UI surfaces stalls well
before the transport notices — radio silence on mobile looks exactly
like a healthy idle socket.

members.name: SetHeartbeatInterval
members.doc: Heartbeat cadence; the backend expects ~15 s.

members.doc: client-side correlation id

members.doc: the envelope "data" (already-serialized JSON)

members.name: OnState
members.signature: std::function<void(const std::string& state, uint64_t version)> OnState
members.doc:
Fired when a snapshot is accepted (in order). The payload is the
server state verbatim — this class never interprets it.

members.name: OnRollback
members.signature: std::function<void(uint64_t localId, const std::string& reason)> OnRollback
members.doc:
Fired when the server rejects an intent: roll the optimistic render
back to the last accepted snapshot.

members.name: ApplySnapshot
members.signature: bool ApplySnapshot(uint64_t version, const std::string& state)
members.doc:
Returns false (and drops) when the snapshot is stale or duplicate:
versions are totally ordered and the server pushes whole states, so
anything <= the last accepted version carries no information.

members.name: OnReject
members.doc:
The reject names the oldest in-flight intent (this protocol answers
intents in order). Everything queued after it stays queued — the
caller decides whether to also drop dependents.

members.name: QueueIntent
members.doc: Queue an intent for sending. Returns the local correlation id.

members.name: TakeSendable
members.doc:
Everything ready to go on the wire. Empty while disconnected — the
outbox holds, nothing is dropped. Sent intents move to the in-flight
list until the matching snapshot (acceptance) or reject arrives.

members.name: ClearInflightThrough
members.doc:
A snapshot acknowledges every intent the server has folded in: with
whole-state pushes there is no per-intent ack, so acceptance = the
next accepted snapshot. Call after ApplySnapshot returns true.

members.name: ConsumeResyncRequest
members.doc:
True once after a (re)connect: the caller sends a `resync` envelope
and the gateway answers with full current state.

members.name: Disconnected
members.doc: never connected, or after Close()

members.name: Closed
members.doc: server sent CLOSE (graceful)

members.name: Failed
members.doc: transport error — see GetError()

members.name: Connect
members.signature: bool Connect(const std::string& url, const std::vector<std::string>& headers = {}, long timeoutSeconds = 15)
members.doc:
Blocking HTTP upgrade to ws:// or wss://. Extra headers are raw
"Name: value" lines (e.g. an auth token when the gateway wants it in a
header rather than the query string).

members.name: Poll
members.doc:
Non-blocking pump: drains everything the socket has, reassembles
fragmented frames, answers PINGs, queues complete messages. Call once
per tick. State moves to Closed/Failed here, never mid-Receive.

members.name: Receive
members.doc: Pop one complete message. Returns false when the queue is empty.

members.name: SendBinary
members.signature: bool SendBinary(const void* data, size_t size)

members.name: Close
members.doc: Sends a CLOSE frame when still connected, then tears down.
